transcript:
Header: 2026-04-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions), Jasmine Lee (Acero Head of ML Infra), Carlos Mendes (Platform Eng), Ruth Okafor (CTO), Marta Ruiz (SRE)

Summary: technical deep dive on observability and tracing integration how Redwood surfaces token-level metrics, OpenTelemetry spans/attributes, dashboards for latency and throughput, and what we need for a pilot in their VPC/dedicated environment. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; heavy focus on token-level cost attribution and KV cache visibility.

Topics: OpenTelemetry span model, token-level metrics, sampling strategies, trace context propagation across gateway & runtime, KV cache hit/miss telemetry, batching and queuing latency visibility, quantization impact on perf, dashboards and SLOs, VPC/on-prem telemetry constraints, compliance for audit logs.

00:00:03 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros  we'll do a short agenda then jump into the observability details.
00:00:18 Jasmine Lee: Thanks Alex, yeah we're really interested in how we can get token-level visibility. Our finance team wants per-feature token costing and SLOs for 99th.
00:00:32 Priya Kapoor: Great, we'll cover how we emit token metrics as OTEL metrics and spans; also how we map tokens to costs and per-route breakdowns.
00:00:47 Carlos Mendes: Quick one  we run in a VPC for PHI, so any telemetry export needs to be compatible with our OTEL collector in the subnet, ideally no egress to public endpoints.
00:01:02 Alex Chen: Totally, that's a common pattern. Redwood Private/Dedicated can push to your collector or we can expose agent endpoints inside your VPC, no egress required.
00:01:18 Ruth Okafor: Also curious about how token-level data interacts with KV cache hits  we don't want to overcount tokens that are saved in cache.

00:02:05 Priya Kapoor: Good point. High level: we instrument the runtime to emit per-request spans with attributes: model_version, seq_len_input, tokens_generated, batching_group, kv_cache_hit (true/false), quantization_profile, gpu_id. We also emit cumulative token metrics per route and per-model.
00:02:28 Priya Kapoor: The KV cache is annotated as a sub-span when a cache lookup happens; if a prefix KV hit is found we emit kv_cache_hit=true and token_generation span is shortened  that shows up in trace duration and token counts.
00:02:50 Marta Ruiz: Sorry can you repeat the attribute names? Our OTEL mapping requires snake_case and specific keys.
00:03:05 Priya Kapoor: Sure  example attributes we send: model.version, request.seq_len, response.tokens_generated, runtime.kv_cache_hit, runtime.batching_group, runtime.quant_profile, runtime.gpu_id. We can parameterize the key names to match your collector mapping.

00:04:20 Alex Chen: Quick architecture diagram, Priya  can you walk through where spans are created? Gateway, router, runtime?
00:04:33 Priya Kapoor: Yes. We create a parent span at the API gateway level (redwood.request) capturing route, customer_id, client_id. Then a child span for routing/placement (redwood.routing) which includes chosen capacity tier (hosted/dedicated/variant). The runtime emits per-token-slice spans: redwood.runtime.token_batch that cover batching windows. When the KV cache is consulted, we emit a redwood.runtime.kv_lookup span. The token generation span measures LM forward latency.
00:05:06 Carlos Mendes: Token-slice spans  we care about those because we want to correlate spikes in 99th latency with batching behavior.
00:05:17 Priya Kapoor: Exactly, the token_batch spans include batching_size and wait_time attributes, so you can create dashboards that show how increased batching correlates with throughput and 99th latency.

00:06:10 Jasmine Lee: A lot of our requests have variable sequence lengths  can you show how sequence length distribution is surfaced?
00:06:22 Priya Kapoor: We emit histograms: request.seq_len.histogram and response.tokens_generated.histogram, plus a token_length_percentiles metric. Also we tag traces with seq_len so you can filter traces >512 tokens.
00:06:48 Ruth Okafor: On the compliance side, how much PII ends up in the telemetry? We need to ensure traces don't leak PHI.
00:06:58 Alex Chen: Redwood supports PII scrubbing in telemetry and the OTEL exporter can be configured to drop attributes or hash them. For Private deployments you control the collector config and we can disable content-level attributes.

00:08:12 Priya Kapoor: Regarding sampling  for token-level cost attribution you want high fidelity metrics but you don't need to store full payloads for every request. Our recommendation: keep full telemetry for a small fraction of production (5-10%) for traces, while emitting aggregated token metrics at 100% fidelity. That gives accurate cost numbers without exploding trace storage.
00:08:45 Carlos Mendes: So aggregated token metrics are per-request counters? If they're 100% we can compute cost by multiplying tokens by per-token-rate.
00:08:58 Priya Kapoor: Yes. We emit per-request response.tokens_generated as an OTEL metric with labels [customer_id, route, model.version, quant_profile]. You can aggregate per-customer and multiply by your pricing rules.

00:10:12 Marta Ruiz: How do you handle quantized models in metrics? We saw that quantization reduces latency but sometimes increases variance in tail latencies.
00:10:27 Priya Kapoor: We include runtime.quant_profile in both spans and metrics so you can pivot. We also have a quantization_performance dataset that correlates quant_profile -> tokens/sec and 99th latency. In the console we show side-by-side charts for different quant profiles.

00:11:40 Alex Chen: Let's talk dashboards  what do customers typically build?
00:11:48 Priya Kapoor: Typical dashboards: per-route token consumption over time, 99/95/50 latency per model version, batching size and wait_time distributions, KV cache hit-rate heatmap by prefix length, GPU utilization by tenant, and anomaly alerts on sudden token cost changes.
00:12:12 Jasmine Lee: For our finance team  we'd need per-feature tagging so feature owners can see cost. Can Redwood propagate our internal feature tags through the request?
00:12:25 Alex Chen: Yes, you can pass custom attributes (e.g., feature=triage_assist) that we include in spans and metrics. On Private, you can enforce allowed custom attribute keys to avoid cardinality explosions.

00:13:40 Carlos Mendes: About trace context propagation  we have our own front-door and want to correlate app traces with Redwood traces. How does context get passed?
00:13:52 Priya Kapoor: We respect W3C traceparent; the gateway will accept incoming trace context and attach it as parent. We also emit a header redwood-trace-id that you can use.

00:14:35 Ruth Okafor: Any concerns with overhead  emitting token-level metrics at 100% could add CPU or network overhead.
00:14:47 Priya Kapoor: The metrics are lightweight counters and histograms. The heavier piece is full traces with payloads. That's why our approach is 100% aggregated metrics + sampled traces. For on-prem/VPC we can batch OTEL exports locally to reduce egress.

00:16:10 Alex Chen: Let's run through a concrete example: a request hits gateway, is routed to dedicated pool, the runtime checks KV cache (hit), does a small generation, returns. Show what you'd see in traces and dashboards.
00:16:24 Priya Kapoor: Example trace: redwood.request (duration 120ms) -> redwood.routing (20ms) -> redwood.runtime.kv_lookup (5ms, runtime.kv_cache_hit=true) -> redwood.runtime.token_batch (wait_time=12ms, batch_size=4) -> redwood.runtime.forward (duration 60ms, response.tokens_generated=12, runtime.quant_profile=int8-gguf). Metrics: request.count=1, response.tokens_generated=12, runtime.kv_cache_hits=1.
00:17:05 Marta Ruiz: That kv_cache_hit flag is key for us, because if hits are high effective tokens consumed is lower for billing.

00:18:20 Priya Kapoor: Regarding batching  we expose batching_group as an attribute. For long-tail requests batching can hurt 99th; on Dedicated you can enforce max_batch_wait=5ms per-tenant. We also surface queue_length metrics so you can set alerts when queueing grows beyond threshold.

00:19:10 Jasmine Lee: How do you recommend setting SLOs for the 99th token latency? We want to guarantee a 99th <= 250ms for our chat flows.
00:19:23 Priya Kapoor: Combine trace-derived percentiles with synthetic probes. Use metric: runtime.forward.latency p99 filtered by route+model.version+quant_profile and alert when it crosses 250ms. Also use Smoke probes to catch regressions in KV cache efficiency.

00:20:02 Carlos Mendes: We run mixed workloads  some high throughput short queries, some long completions. Can Redwood attribute costs per-route and per-product?
00:20:14 Alex Chen: Yes, route-level attributes plus custom feature tags let you slice costs. In Dedicated we can also provide a usage export (CSV/parquet) with token counts per-route per-hour.

00:21:10 Priya Kapoor: Implementation details: our runtime uses OTEL SDK to push metrics and spans to an exporter. For Hosted we push to our telemetry backend and mirror metrics to your OTEL collector if configured. For Private we ship an OTEL exporter that writes to your collector endpoint inside the VPC.

00:22:05 Marta Ruiz: Any specific OTEL versions or gotchas? We run collector v0.51.
00:22:17 Priya Kapoor: We're compatible with OTEL collector >=0.45; the only gotcha is you need to configure attribute sanitization to avoid high cardinality tags from user-supplied metadata. We can provide a reference collector config.

00:23:40 Alex Chen: What about dashboards  do you recommend Grafana/Honeycomb/Datadog?
00:23:50 Priya Kapoor: Many customers use Grafana + Prometheus for aggregated metrics, plus Honeycomb for high-cardinality trace exploration. Datadog/Splunk are supported through exporters. If you already have a data plane we can integrate.

00:24:45 Ruth Okafor: For our security review, we need proof that telemetry doesn't leak content  do you have SOC2 controls around telemetry?
00:24:58 Alex Chen: Yes we can share our security pack; for Private deployments telemetry export is under your control and we can disable content attributes. We'll attach a security + compliance bundle in the follow-up.

00:26:30 Priya Kapoor: A note on token counting: we use the model tokenizer semantics to compute tokens_generated; for multi-model setups tokenization differences are exposed with model.tokenizer_kind attribute. We also emit estimated input_tokens and output_tokens separately.

00:27:10 Carlos Mendes: Is the tokenizer calculation deterministic across releases? We need stable billing.
00:27:22 Priya Kapoor: We pin model versions and record tokenizer changes as part of model.version metadata. If tokenization semantics change we emit previous_version and new_version and have metrics to show delta. We've seen this in a couple of upstream model updates.

00:28:55 Alex Chen: Let's touch on quantization again  customers saw latency gains but sometimes the 99th got worse. Any guidance?
00:29:06 Priya Kapoor: Quantization reduces compute per-token but can increase variability; we recommend staging different quant profiles and measuring p50/p95/p99. In the console we provide quant_profile comparisons and a suggested default per-workload. Also, for very latency-sensitive routes we allow pinning to fp16.

00:30:35 Marta Ruiz: Regarding observability in on-prem  if we deploy Redwood Private on our k8s, do we still run the OTEL collector ourselves or you provide one?
00:30:49 Priya Kapoor: You run your collector  we provide Helm charts and example configs. The runtime sidecar emits OTEL and pushes to the local collector endpoint. No telemetry leaves your cluster unless you configure an external exporter.

00:31:30 Carlos Mendes: For the pilot we want a benchmark: 10k requests/s sustained with 3 different seq_len profiles, measure tokens/sec, p99 latency, and KV cache hit rate. Can Redwood run that in Dedicated?
00:31:46 Alex Chen: Yes, we can set up a Dedicated pilot pool and run the benchmark. We'll need sample request profiles and a target SLA. We'll coordinate on infra access.

00:32:20 Priya Kapoor: For AVAIL metrics: GPU_util, runtime.queue_length, batch.wait_time.histogram, response.tokens_generated.histogram, runtime.kv_cache_hit_rate (ratio), and trace-derived forward.latency.p99  these are the key signals for pilot success.

00:33:05 Jasmine Lee: One more  do you surface per-token embedding compute separately? We have embedding endpoints too and want separate billing.
00:33:18 Priya Kapoor: Yes embeddings have distinct metrics: embedding.tokens_processed and embedding.time_per_request. We tag by model.family so you can separate generative vs embedding costs.

00:34:40 Alex Chen: Let's simulate a failure mode  high 99th latency due to sudden batching  what alarms?
00:34:53 Priya Kapoor: Alerts: runtime.batch.wait_time.p95 > X ms, queue_length > Y, forward.latency.p99 increase > 2x baseline. Also correlate with kv_cache_hit_rate drops. In our console you can create composite alerts that join these signals.

00:35:40 Carlos Mendes: About telemetry volume and storage  if traces are sampled and metrics are aggregated, what's the expected cardinality and size?
00:35:53 Priya Kapoor: Metrics cardinality depends on label set; key avoiders are uncontrolled user tags. For traces sampled at 5% and metrics at 100% aggregated, storage is roughly X GB per 1M requests (we included an estimate in the pilot doc we'll send). We'll share specifics for your traffic profile.

00:36:50 Ruth Okafor: Are there any open source pieces we can reuse? We already use OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Prometheus.
00:37:02 Priya Kapoor: Yes; our OTEL integration is standard. For dashboards we share Grafana dashboards and Prometheus recording rules. We also have a Honeycomb quickstart.

00:38:20 Alex Chen: Let's call out the items we'll deliver post call. Priya?
00:38:26 Priya Kapoor: We'll send: OTEL attribute mapping doc, example collector config for v0.51, Grafana dashboards (JSON), benchmarking instructions & SOW template.

00:39:05 Jasmine Lee: Great. For the SOW, can you include a line item for telemetry integration and collector support?
00:39:14 Alex Chen: Yes we'll include that in pricing.

00:40:00 Priya Kapoor: Quick aside  some words in the transcript might be messy; the runtime emits a lot of attributes but we recommend limiting high-card keys.

00:40:30 Carlos Mendes: Any notes on correlation IDs for billing? We need a stable key we can join on.
00:40:42 Priya Kapoor: Use customer_id + request_id; we emit both as labels and a redwood_trace_id header. For batch aggregation we also expose batch_id so you can reconcile.

00:41:55 Marta Ruiz: For the KV cache heatmap  do you expose prefix length buckets?
00:42:06 Priya Kapoor: Yes, runtime.kv_prefix_len bucketed metrics and hit_rate per bucket. That helps tune cache TTLs and prefetch policies.

00:43:30 Alex Chen: Ok let's open for any final technical questions.
00:43:36 Ruth Okafor: What's the recommended OTEL exporter format for low latency? OTLP/gRPC or HTTP?
00:43:47 Priya Kapoor: OTLP/gRPC is preferred for performance; OTLP/HTTP is ok but adds overhead. Inside VPC choose gRPC to your collector endpoint.

00:44:20 Carlos Mendes: For the Dedicated pilot, will you provide a dedicated prometheus endpoint or push gateway?
00:44:33 Alex Chen: We can provision a Prometheus scrape target inside the Dedicated network or push metrics to your existing Prometheus via a Pushgateway. We usually recommend scrape targets for reliability.

00:45:10 Jasmine Lee: Any expectation for data retention on metrics we get? We prefer 13 months for cost analysis.

00:45:21 Alex Chen: Retention is configurable for Private; for Hosted we have tiers (90 days default, 13 months as add-on). We'll include retention options in the proposal.

00:46:05 Priya Kapoor: One more technical caveat  if you enable debug-level spans with payload digests, even hashed content can increase cardinality; we suggest limiting debug spans to a small percentage.

00:47:00 Alex Chen: Alright we'll wrap with next steps. Summarize?
00:47:08 Jasmine Lee: Provide OTEL mapping, sample profiles, and pilot SOW; we'll respond with CSV of token lengths.

00:47:20 Alex Chen: Sounds good. Thanks all.

00:48:00 End of call notes: Follow ups scheduled; overall interest high in Dedicated pilot with focus on telemetry integration and token-level billing.
